title: What If You Could See the Oldest Light in the Universe?

scenes.text: What if you could see the Big Bang? A faint glow of it fills every direction.
It is called the cosmic microwave background, light released about 380,000 years after the Big Bang.
Before then, the universe was too hot and dense for light to travel freely.
Today that light has cooled to just 2.725 degrees above absolute zero.
Two Bell Labs engineers found it in 1965 while chasing noise in a horn antenna.
Tune an old analog TV between channels, and a small part of that static is this ancient glow.
